messages:
anya: Noticing a recurring p95 token latency spike on the KV-heavy models over the last 2 hours, correlated with eviction churn. Root p95 up ~200-300ms
mike: Yup saw that too. Digging into perf: flame shows a big hot path in evicter::reinsert under high paging load
samir: Can you paste the flame? also which eviction policy was live on the affected pool (LRU/FIFO)?
anya: Pool is using LRU by default. Flame (shortened):
```
hot: evicter::reinsert (62%)
  evicter::steal_slot
  kv_shard::lock_and_evict
  kv_page::serialize_for_swap
```
mike: Interesting, evicter is holding shard lock while doing serialization -> blocking lookups. That matches latency spikes
kat: We instrumented lock hold times last week. There was a median_hold ~1.2ms but tail to 150ms under pressure. Might be the serialization step blowing the tail up
anya: Logs from one node: `evict_start shard=7 victim=0x7f2d9 hold_ms=142 serialize_ms=120`
mike: That ties directly to p95. Two suspects: (1) reinsert order interactions when LRU updates collide, (2) IO/serialization cost during swapback. Which one is driving the long hold?
samir: I ran a microbench: mix of long-context requests (avg seq 2048) + bursty arrivals. Reproducer: `./bench --kv-entries 1M --seq 2048 --policy lru --burst 500` gives similar spike in ~30s
kat: Can we try policy switch? If FIFO avoids reinsert skews we can mitigate immediately while we dig correctness
anya: Quick test on staging: switched shard group 4->FIFO, p95 dropped ~90ms but throughput slightly down. So FIFO helps latency but we need to ensure correctness for reuse semantics
mike: Right—our correctness invariants assume LRU-based timestamp monotonicity for reuse heuristics. FIFO could increase cache churn for some workloads
samir: There's also a subtle reinsert race: when entry A is evicted and immediately reinserted by a concurrent request, the LRU timestamp update path runs while evicter still holds a reference. If ordering flips we can end with stale indices causing extra work (double-reclaim attempts seen in logs)
anya: Example log snippet: `reinsert: id=0xabc old_ts=159345 new_ts=159340 -> out-of-order, scheduling reserialize`
kat: That 'scheduling reserialize' is the expensive path. If we can decouple serialization from shard lock (serialize out-of-band) we can reduce hold_ms significantly
mike: Agreed. Two-pronged plan: short-term: selective FIFO on hot shards to bring p95 down. medium-term: refactor evict path to do serialization without holding shard lock (handoff queue). Also add instrumentation for reinsert-order inversions
samir: I'll open a PR for the instrumentation and a perf test harness to repro the inversion. I'll also add counters: evict_reinsert_order_inversions, evict_hold_ms_hist per shard
anya: I'll prepare a canary config to flip policy for the top-3 effected shards and watch for correctness regressions in acceptance tests
kat: One more idea: adaptive backoff on reinsert when we detect immediate reaccess (cheap quick check) to avoid bouncing between evict/reinsert
mike: Good. If it works, low-risk change. But need to validate under mixed-ttl workloads
pagerduty-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3412345678 - KV eviction latency spike (assigned eng-runtime) :rotating_light:
anya: Thanks. Samir / Mike please coordinate on the PRs. I'll roll the FIFO canary and monitor. Ping here with links to diffs
mike: Will do. PR drafts by EOD. Samir will attach perf traces
samir: Uploaded initial perf trace to the shared bucket: gs://redwood-perf/3412345678/trace.pb.gz. Repro steps in the README inside the bucket.
anya: Nice, I'll start the FIFO canary now. Updating channel with progress. :eyes:
